bio: Richard Brinsley Sheridan was born in Dublin and became one of the leading English-language dramatists of his century, the author of The Rivals and The School for Scandal. He was also manager of the Drury Lane Theatre and a Whig Member of Parliament.
The song "Thou canst not boast" is included in W. B. Yeats's A Book of Irish Verse (1900).

poems.title: Thou Canst Not Boast
poems.author: Richard Brinsley Sheridan
poems.collection: A Book of Irish Verse, ed. W. B. Yeats (1900)
poems.text:
Thou canst not boast of Fortune's store,
  My love, while me they wealthy call:
But I was glad to find thee poor,
  For with my heart I'd give thee all,
    And then the grateful youth shall own,
    I loved him for himself alone.

But when his worth my hand shall gain,
  No word or look of mine shall show
That I the smallest thought retain
  Of what my bounty did bestow:
    Yet still his grateful heart shall own,
    I loved him for himself alone.
